facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Asilisaurus kongwe.
facts.quote: The type species is Asilisaurus kongwe.

facts.statement: Some authors suggest the Manda Beds formation may date to the Ladinian or early Carnian stages instead of the Anisian.
facts.quote: some authors assert that the formation may be Ladinian or early Carnian instead

facts.statement: Asilisaurus was the first non-dinosaur dinosauromorph recovered from Africa.
facts.quote: Asilisaurus was the first (ostensibly) non-dinosaur dinosauromorph recovered from Africa.

facts.statement: Asilisaurus had a unique lack of teeth at the front of the premaxilla and a downturned, toothless tip on its lower jaw.
facts.quote: It had several unique features compared to its close relatives, such as a lack of teeth at the front of the premaxilla and a lower jaw which was not only toothless at the tip, but also downturned.

facts.statement: Asilisaurus was described in 2010 by a team of researchers from the United States, Germany, and South Africa.
facts.quote: Asilisaurus was described in 2010 by a team of researchers from the United States, Germany, and South Africa, in the journal Nature.

facts.statement: The generic name Asilisaurus is derived from the Swahili word for 'ancestor' and the Greek word for 'lizard'.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from asili, the Swahili word for "ancestor" or "foundation", as well as σαυρος (sauros), the Greek word for "lizard".

facts.statement: The specific name kongwe means 'ancient' in Swahili.
facts.quote: The specific name kongwe is in line with this naming scheme, as it is the Swahili word for "ancient".

facts.statement: The first remains of Asilisaurus were found in 2007 at a bonebed near Litumba Ndyosi in Tanzania.
facts.quote: The first remains of Asilisaurus were found in 2007 at "locality Z34", a bonebed near the town of Litumba Ndyosi in Tanzania.

facts.statement: At least 14 individuals of Asilisaurus were present at the discovery site, including the holotype.
facts.quote: At least 14 individuals were present at the site, including NMT RB9, the holotype dentary.

facts.statement: Asilisaurus was a lightly built animal with a long neck, short beaked snout, and slender limbs.
facts.quote: Asilisaurus was a lightly built animal with a fairly long neck (by early archosaur standards), a short snout tipped with a beak, and slender limbs.

facts.statement: Based on limb length, Asilisaurus probably walked on all four legs.
facts.quote: It probably walked on all four legs based on the length of its limbs.

facts.statement: Asilisaurus specimens are estimated to be 1 to 3 meters long, 0.5 to 1 meter high at the hip, and weigh 10 to 30 kilograms.
facts.quote: Asilisaurus specimens have been estimated to measure from 1 to 3 m long and 0.5 to 1 m high at the hip, and may have weighed 10 to 30 kg.

facts.statement: One femur specimen was estimated to be 29.6-39.6 cm long, more than twice the length of other known Asilisaurus femurs.
facts.quote: This femur had an estimated length of 29.6-39.6 cm (11.7-15.6 in), more than twice the length of the next largest Asilisaurus femurs.

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Asilisaurus had only a single tooth at the rear near the maxilla.
facts.quote: There is only a single tooth at the rear of the bone, near the contact with the maxilla.

facts.statement: Asilisaurus teeth were conical, pointed, and slightly recurved.
facts.quote: The teeth are conical, pointed, and slightly recurved.

facts.statement: The front tip of the jugal bone was pointed, wedging between the lacrimal and maxilla.
facts.quote: The front tip of the jugal is pointed, wedging between a wide lower branch of the lacrimal and a presumably sloping rear portion of the maxilla.

facts.statement: The front of the dentary was toothless and curved into a downward-pointing tip, unlike other silesaurids.
facts.quote: Like the premaxilla, the front of the dentary is toothless and curves into a point. The tip bends down, in contrast to other silesaurids where it bends up.

facts.statement: Asilisaurus had two sacral vertebrae with individual sacral ribs, contrasting with Silesaurus which has three or four sharing ribs.
facts.quote: There were two sacral vertebrae, each with its own sacral ribs. This contrasts with Silesaurus, which has three or four sacral vertebrae which share sacral ribs between each other.

facts.statement: The Asilisaurus scapula was long, narrow, and expanded into a triangular tip without perforations.
facts.quote: The scapula (shoulder blade) is long and narrow, expanded into a triangular structure at the tip and lacking any perforations on the acromion process.

facts.statement: The Asilisaurus radius was thin, simple, and about 85% the length of the humerus.
facts.quote: The radius is thin and simple, similar in shape to that of Herrerasaurus. However, it was also shorter than the humerus, only about 85% the length of that bone.

facts.statement: Asilisaurus possessed a closed acetabulum in its hip, distinguishing it from the open acetabulum found in dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Asilisaurus's hip had a closed acetabulum, rather than the open acetabulum of dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The claws (unguals) of Asilisaurus were low and wide, giving them a hoof-like appearance similar to Silesaurus and shuvosaurids.
facts.quote: Unguals were low and wide, a "hoof"-like appearance also seen in Silesaurus and the unrelated shuvosaurids.

facts.statement: Evidence of a beak and peg-like teeth suggests Asilisaurus was likely an omnivore or herbivore.
facts.quote: Evidence for a beak at the tip of the snout and peg-like teeth further back support the idea that Asilisaurus was an omnivore or herbivore.

facts.statement: The conical shape of Asilisaurus's teeth suggests that fish may have been part of its diet.
facts.quote: The conical shape of the teeth shares some similarities with piscivorous reptiles such as spinosaurids and crocodilians, leading to the possibility that fish were part of its diet.

facts.statement: Research indicates Asilisaurus was unlikely to be a specialized carnivore or an obligate herbivore.
facts.quote: Regardless, Asilisaurus was very unlikely to be a specialized carnivore like the more basal silesaurid Lewisuchus, nor an obligate herbivore like Kwanasaurus.

facts.statement: Studies of Asilisaurus femurs revealed multiple polymorphic trajectories in muscle scar development rather than a universal sequence.
facts.quote: The study found that there was no universal sequence, and instead multiple polymorphic trajectories, with many traits appearing earlier in the sequence in some bones and later in others.

facts.statement: Histological analysis of Asilisaurus bones showed no lines of arrested growth (LAGs), even in large specimens.
facts.quote: No LAGs (lines of arrested growth) are observed, even in bones from large individuals.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that the absence of LAGs in Asilisaurus does not mean specimens died within a year, as their growth rate was too slow for that.
facts.quote: It is hypothesized that a lack of LAGs is not indicative that all the specimens died within a year, as the estimated growth rate is not fast enough to achieve skeletal maturity within that time period.

facts.statement: Asilisaurus is the first non-dinosaur dinosauriform discovered in Africa.
